title: DHCP UI Overhaul (pfSense-style) (v1)
acceptance_criteria: Network -> DHCP shows interface-based options for enabling DHCP only on interfaces with a configured static IPv4 address.
Interface options display the interface description/name (pfSense-like), not just raw interface IDs.
When creating a DHCP server for an interface, the default range is pre-populated within the interface subnet (and is adjustable).
UI validates that the DHCP range is inside the interface subnet and does not overlap the interface IP or broadcast/network addresses.
Backend apply is idempotent (re-applying the same config does not error) and surfaces actionable validation errors.
Automated tests exist for default range calculation + backend apply payload generation.
assumptions: v1 targets IPv4 DHCP server only (not DHCPv6).
Eligible interfaces are those with a configured static IPv4 address (not DHCP).
Default range selection will be conservative (avoid .1/.0/.255), and may need Mark confirmation for non-/24 subnets.

tasks.notes: Produce Feature Spec Packet (UX flow, interface eligibility, default range algorithm, VyOS semantics).
Convert spec into implementation plan, milestones, rollback plan, and test strategy.
Add/extend endpoints to list eligible interfaces + compute defaults; ensure RBAC and validation.
Overhaul DHCP page UX (pfSense-like interface selection + guided defaults) without breaking existing config editing.
Add automated tests for default range logic + backend request validation; run locally and document results.
Review for security (RBAC), correctness, edge cases (odd subnets), and regression risk.
Update docs and verification steps; prep PR summary.

backlog.title: IPsec Site-to-Site VPN Wizard (v1)
acceptance_criteria: Wizard can create one site-to-site IPsec tunnel (Phase 1 + Phase 2) from UI with minimal inputs.
Wizard configures required firewall/NAT so traffic flows (IKE/ESP/NAT-T as applicable).
Wizard is idempotent or clearly warns before overwriting config it created.
Wizard failures surface actionable errors and avoid silently leaving partial config.
Automated tests exist for backend parsing/build/apply logic.
assumptions: v1 targets IPv4, IKEv2, PSK auth, single tunnel.
Default mode (policy-based vs VTI) is TBD; must be confirmed by Mark.
Wizard-created config will be tagged with a stable description/prefix for detection and cleanup.
